narrative.overview:
The console does not have a visual identity of its own. It is the SSEC design system (University of Washington Scientific Software Engineering Center) applied to an administration tool. Every colour, type size, line height and letter spacing comes from a pinned, unmodified copy of the upstream tokens at `services/console/frontend/src/styles/ssec-tokens.css` (upstream `design-system/01-tokens.css`, branch `staging`, commit `d3f017b`, 2026-09-11). Upstream marks that system alpha, which is why the copy is pinned. The values in the frontmatter above are that copy's values under the names the console's theme gives them (`src/index.css`); they are a record, and the token file stays the source. To change a value, re-copy the token file; do not edit it and do not restate a value by hand.

What this document adds is how the console uses the system: a Husky Purple sidebar, a white top bar, and a warm gold ground carrying white cards. The pages are ledgers. Figures sit in one divided strip, lists are tables, and the form that adds to a list sits in its own card beside it. Density is moderate: 14 to 15px table text, 24px between cards, 24px inside them. Three roles use the same shell and the same components; a screen differs by what it lists, never by how it looks.

The system is light theme only. Nothing sets the `dark` class, and the theme's `dark:` variant is tied to that class so that the operating system's setting changes nothing. No chart, sparkline or trend chip exists, because the data behind one does not exist yet. The content security policy allows no inline style and no style element added at run time, so overlays are built on the browser's own `<dialog>` element and the select is the browser's own `<select>`.
keyCharacteristics: A pinned copy of upstream tokens; the console defines no colours of its own.
One shell for every signed-in screen: 256px sidebar, 56px top bar, page.
One signature: a 2px teal line that marks where you are.
Square buttons, 8px cards, hairline borders, almost no shadow.
Uppercase compressed Encode Sans for every label; sentence case for all else.
Tables that become lists of records when their card is too narrow.

rules.name: The Teal Line Rule
rules.body: On a light surface, teal appears only as the 2px line that says where you are or that a page is on its way. It is never a fill, a text colour or a button there. Teal on white is under 2:1, so the line never carries a state alone: the current tab also changes from Secondary Ink to Spirit Purple and carries `aria-current`.

rules.name: The Borrowed Palette Rule
rules.body: A colour is used through a theme name (`primary`, `nav`, `page`, `signature`), and every theme name points at an upstream token. A hex value written into a component is a defect.

rules.name: The Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase compressed type labels a control or a piece of data that sits right next to it: a column, a field, a figure, a tab, a button. It is never set above a heading as a category line.

rules.name: The Typed Things Rule
rules.body: If a client or a person has to type it exactly, it is in mono. If not, it is not.

rules.name: The Border First Rule
rules.body: A card is drawn by its hairline; the shadow only softens it. A surface that needs a larger shadow to be seen is floating, and only notices, dialogs and the signed-out card float.

dos: Do take every colour, size, line height and tracking value from a theme name that points at the pinned upstream token file.
Do build a new screen from the existing parts in the existing order: page title, stat strip, optional tabs, cards.
Do mark the current place with the 2px teal line together with a change of text colour and `aria-current`.
Do keep buttons square and everything else that has a surface at 8px, with 12px for dialogs and tags.
Do set labels of columns, fields, figures, tabs and buttons in the uppercase compressed style, and everything else in sentence case.
Do put the form that adds to a list in its own card beside that list, and let the split stack it underneath when the container is under 68rem.
Do give each table the container width under which it becomes records, so a row's actions never leave the screen.
Do say what an irreversible action does in the card that holds its button, and ask again in a dialog.
Do build an overlay on the native `<dialog>` element and lock the page behind it with a class.
donts: Don't edit `ssec-tokens.css` or write a hex value into a component.
Don't add dark-theme styles. The console is light only, by decision.
Don't draw a chart, a sparkline, a trend arrow or a placeholder for one. A figure on screen is one the server sent.
Don't use teal as a fill, a text colour or a button on a light surface, or as the only sign of a state.
Don't use a component that inserts a style element or an inline style at run time. The content security policy refuses it, which rules out the Radix dialog, select and sheet.
Don't round a button, and don't add a shadow to a button or to a hover state.
Don't set the uppercase label style above a heading as a category line.
Don't tag the ordinary state. `active` shows nothing.
Don't turn the stat strip into separate tiles, or add a second strip to a page.
